title: S03 phase 2/3: Village tutorial ladder: Tam's tools -> team of five -> training -> gathering -> camp + creature bed -> sleep -> feed
_comment: Transcribed from docs/acceptance/GATE_F_MASTER_PROTOCOL.md section B (span), section D (RT-02), section E.1 (CB-02), section E.3 (S03 builds the tutorial home and three creature beds under the real economy, free_build OFF), section E.5 (navigation record at each of the eight main-chain objectives this segment crosses), section G (GF-03-VILLAGE-02, GF-18-MAP-01, GF-20-NIGHT-01/02, GF-14-COMBAT-02) and section H (0.1 Hz segment).
_comment_economy: Section E.3: 'The authoritative run keeps free_build OFF everywhere'. Nothing in this file touches the Settings toggle; the camp and the creature bed are paid for out of the twenty village harvest nodes walked below. The real bill, read from data/items/buildables.json through scripts/build/home_progress.gd::materials_threshold(), is camp (12 wood / 8 stone / 10 fiber) plus one creature_bed (6 wood / 8 fiber) = 18 / 8 / 18. One sweep of the twenty nodes yields 28 / 9 / 32, so the budget clears with +10 wood, +1 stone and +14 fiber. The stone margin is ONE node wide and is the number to watch: the village authors only three stone nodes, and until GAME-F1 was fixed one of them stood outside the fence, which put reachable stone at 6 against a bill of 8.
_comment_catalogue: AMBIGUITY: the protocol does not enumerate S03's build-catalogue navigation (section E.3 step 2 enumerates X02's 2x2 lab structure, not S03's home). The focus counts below are derived from data/items/buildables.json's category order and build_menu.gd's CATEGORY_ORDER, and from build_menu.gd remembering the last category and piece per session. They are a transcriber's derivation, not the protocol's words, and a focus_move that does not land FAILs loudly rather than silently selecting the wrong piece.
_comment_answer_prompts: answer_prompts stays OFF on every walk, per the schema's rule.
_comment_evidence_lane: §H/§G evidence split, owner decision 2026-08-27, recorded in docs/acceptance/GATE_F_MASTER_PROTOCOL.md §H.1. This is the LOGIC lane: the journey run headless for mechanics, telemetry and step verdicts at 6.1 ms/frame against 12,721 ms for a rendered frame on the Gate F container. It takes no prescribed frame; the §G ids its steps would have taken are DELEGATED to S03C, which declares each of them in its "owes" list. The harness refuses to start this segment if S03C does not exist, does not declare evidence_lane=capture, or does not accept every id handed to it -- a delegation nobody accepted is a debt that has quietly stopped existing, which is the same shape as the 9,231 file:null PASSes CD-1 was written for. Whether the debt was actually PAID is a question about the whole run directory and is answered by tools/gate_f/run_inventory.py, not here.
_comment_record_hz_split: AMENDED for the §H/§G evidence split. record_hz is forced to 0 on a logic lane by the harness regardless of what this file says, because §H's continuous record is the thing the split removes: the recorder's cadence is counted in PLAY seconds now, but under a 12.7 s rendered frame even a 0.1 Hz record fires on every rendered frame, and the eighteen segments' 4,607,802 physics frames are ~8,283 hours. The obligation is not dropped -- §H's prescribed frames move to S03C, which may run BOUNDED record windows around a named state.

steps.title: T2-BUILDPLACE: why Mira's door has to be opened by hand, and why the ally is re-checked here too

args.text: FINDING-T2-BUILDPLACE-2026-08-30.md, round 3. Two separate things previously blocked this walk, and both are handled now: (1) scripts/combat/encounter_director.gd::interaction_offer()'s blanket "<ally> is out of the fight" override (round 2's finding, still not owned/fixed by this lane -- scripts/combat/** is T3-TYPECHART's) outranks every prompt in the world whenever the tracked `_ally` is fainted. Bryn's fight is now REAL (S03-39b/c), so the ally could have fainted there instead of in the catch loop; `S03-51c` below re-runs the SAME safe party_cycle used before Bryn, for the same reason. (2) The actual, previously undiagnosed cause of every prior round's 'walked near Mira and still got refused/stuck 2-5m short' symptom: OF31 moved Mira INSIDE cottage_a, behind a shut door (data/config/village_npcs.json:47, scripts/world/village_door.gd). A live probe confirmed the door defaults CLOSED (`is_open() == false` at boot) with a real solid `Gate` StaticBody3D collider spanning the doorway (`village_door.gd::setup()`, 1.6m x 2.3m x 0.45m) that a raw physics raycast from outside to inside actually hits -- this blocks BOTH the player's walk (the stick_navigator has no way to open a door, so it slides along the shut leaf and can wander metres off course hunting for a gap that is not there) AND the line-of-sight check Mira's own Interactable prompt needs (interactable.gd::_has_line_of_sight refuses through the same collider), which is why some earlier attempts read as a geometry/LOS problem rather than a closed door. `S03-52`..`S03-52c` below open it first, the same way a real player would (walk up, read 'Open Door', press interact) -- confirmed live end-to-end (tools/gate_f/probe_mira_walk_trace.gd and a standalone segment replay): once open, a straight walk from just outside the door to Mira's own live position converges in well under 100 frames with 0 held, and her real 'Greet Mira' prompt wins immediately.

steps.title: why this training pass exists

args.text: Added 2026-09-02, per direct instruction to close every real S03 FAIL rather than record and stop: `tournament_training_ready` (entry.min_level=5, checked against the full five-creature roster) is a REAL, validated threshold -- OWNER-0901-TRAIN-CLARITY-V2/OWNER-0901-TOURNAMENT-LEVEL5 confirmed it with a real headless test suite and a real simulated tournament win, and objectives.json's own authored guidance already tells the player 'Wins are levels. Get your whole team to level 5' -- not a made-up number this segment invents pacing to satisfy. One Bryn fight alone leaves the team at a uniform level 3 (a ~600 XP/creature gap to level 5, progression.gd's xp_to_next curve). `combat_manager.gd::_award_victory()` pays the active pilot the FULL award and every OTHER non-fainted party member `party_share` (35%) of it on every win -- so a wild fight anywhere trains the whole team at once, not just whoever is piloting, and rotating the pilot between fights (party_cycle below) spreads the full award around instead of stacking it on one creature. The blocks below engage whichever wild bramblebun the catch loop's own ten-attempt ladder did not need (rank 10+, clamping to whatever is actually left the same way the catch loop's own `rank` already does) and fight it to a real resolution -- `fight_until_resolved`, no `until_flag`, so it costs nothing and reports cleanly even on a round that finds nothing left to fight.

steps.title: T2-BUILDPLACE: why the tools need binding by hand

args.text: FINDING-T2-BUILDPLACE-2026-08-30.md: wood/stone/fiber are all tool-gated (harvest_logic.gd, gathered_with) and carrying a tool in the satchel is not enough -- it must be visibly EQUIPPED on the hotbar (tests/test_harvest.gd::test_gather_with_no_equipped_tool_is_refused). Grandpa's opening gift already fills the hotbar (autofill_hotbar fires once, on the very first all-empty poll), so Tam's knife and Mira's axe/pickaxe never land on the bar on their own. The sequence below is the production gesture X02.json's build lab already uses (backpack_assign, L3): open the Satchel, put the cursor on an item, press backpack_assign, which cycles it unbound -> slot 1 -> slot 2 -> ... -> off. Knife (4 presses -> slot 4) and pickaxe (3 -> slot 3) are bound before axe (2 -> slot 2) because a never-before-bound item's FIRST press always lands at slot 1 regardless of what already occupies it. T2-GATEF-RUN5, GAME-9/RIG-24: the three focus steps below used to be `focus_move` press counts (4 right, 3 left, 1 left) derived from a FRESH save's fill order, and both halves of that were wrong here. The bag is not fresh -- run 4's telemetry shows both Revive draughts spent and potions down from three to one before a tool is bound -- and `ui_left` does NOT wrap up a grid row, so from the knife's cell the count walked backwards along row 0 instead of reaching the pickaxe on row 1. Reproduced exactly by tools/gate_f/probe_tool_equip_depleted_bag.gd: the old counts leave the hotbar ["","","potion_small","knife",""] -- which is precisely the {hotbar_slot: 3, item: "knife"} every one of run 4's six real gathers reported -- while `focus_item` on the same bag leaves ["","axe","pickaxe","knife",""]. `focus_item` sends the same real ui_* events; it just reads the cursor between them instead of assuming.

TRADE RECORDED EXPLICITLY: the schema says this flag must stay off in any segment whose subject is whether something blocks travel, so these segments can no longer evidence 'a narrative modal blocked the player from travelling'. That finding is already captured in full, un-answered, in S02-superseded-2/3/4 and S02/BLOCKER.md -- three press counts, identical 7201-frame holds. What it buys is everything downstream: measured in S03 and S04, an unanswered modal at a walk's end left input_context='narrative_modal' where the next step expected combat, so no fight started, no catch resolved, the team never reached three, and every tournament entry check then failed on team size. steps.title: close Oskar's creature swap without trading
steps.expected: S03 does not exercise creature trading (that is X-lab territory); back out to world control with nothing swapped. T2-GATEF-RUN5. Oskar's greeting ends with `shop:creatures:oskar` (data/dialogue/village.json), which sequence_director.gd::_maybe_open_shop() opens as a SwapPanel the moment his dialogue box closes -- exactly the way Mira's greeting opens her goods shop. Mira's is closed by S03-56 and the world re-asserted by S03-56a; Oskar's was never closed at all. Nobody noticed for four sessions because GAME-8 meant the walk to Oskar never arrived and his dialogue never ran. With GAME-8 fixed, this run's telemetry shows `input_context` pinned at 'panel:SwapPanel' from S03-62 to the end of the segment: every hotbar_N press after it was swallowed by playground_hud.gd::_world_input_allowed() (so equipped stayed {hotbar_slot: -1, item: ""} despite a correctly bound bar), and every walk reported '0 held' while never leaving (19,-6), because a panel owning input is not the same thing as locomotion being disabled. Same shape as RIG-13..RIG-22: a real fix closing one gap and the next one behind it becoming visible for the first time.

_comment_stale_rebuild: RIG, 2026-08-31 (lane ralph/GATE-F-LEG-S03). This file was transcribed against a version of the chapter that no longer ships, and most of what GAME-F5 recorded against the gathering economy was this file asking for the wrong building. FIRST-HOUR-FUN-REBUILD changed three shipped numbers and none of them reached here. (1) data/config/tournament.json entry.min_party_size is 5, not 3 -- and it was already 5 on candidate 453107fb, the very SHA the audit measured, so DEFECTS.md's 'tournament.json requires min_party_size: 3' was wrong about its own candidate. data/progression/objectives.json's tournament_build_team says it in words: 'Build your full team of five for the village tournament.' (2) data/config/progression.json home.required_pieces is {camp: 1, creature_bed: 1} -- ONE camp and ONE bed. This file built camp+floor+wall+door+roof and THREE beds and measured the village's gathering budget against that: 45 wood / 17 stone / 34 fiber, against a real requirement of 18 / 8 / 18 that the twenty village nodes (28 / 9 / 32 in one pass) cover with room to spare. (3) The bed rung's flag is creature_bed_built, not creature_bed_built_3; objectives.json calls one bed 'the mandatory care lesson' and tests/test_quest_log.gd asserts the rung 'must not require one bed per tournament entrant'. The floor/wall/door/roof and second/third bed blocks are removed rather than retained-and-skipped: a step that builds something the game does not ask for is not extra coverage, it is a false economy measurement, and that is exactly what GAME-F5 reported.
